claims.statement: canonicalizeMode normalizes the deprecated Mode token "research" to the CanonicalMode "deepresearch" and returns the warning 'Mode "research" is deprecated; use "deepresearch" instead.', which runMode folds into PipelineResult.warnings; every other mode passes through unchanged.

resolveModel(config, profile, alias) is a plain table lookup into config.models[profile][alias]; DEFAULT_MODELS defines the quality and economy profiles each with the five aliases fast, expert, research, deepResearch, nativeMulti, where economy collapses expert to x-ai/grok-4.3 and both research and deepResearch to perplexity/sonar-pro, while quality uses x-ai/grok-4.3 (fast), x-ai/grok-4.20 (expert), perplexity/sonar-reasoning-pro (research), perplexity/sonar-deep-research (deepResearch), x-ai/grok-4.20-multi-agent (nativeMulti).

DEFAULT_CONFIG sets defaultMode to "auto" and defaultProfile to "quality", and resolveCliOptions fills mode and profile from these config defaults only when the CLI did not set them explicitly (modeExplicit/profileExplicit), so --economy and positional/--mode tokens always win over config.

modeAllowsWeb returns true only for the modes auto, fast, expert, and retrieve; deepresearch and multi (and the deprecated research, which is canonicalized to deepresearch before the check) never allow OpenRouter web tools.

resolveWebOptions computes searchEnabled = modeAllowsWeb(mode) AND (retrieve ? true : config.web.search.enabled) AND NOT cli.noWeb, so CLI --no-web overrides config web.search.enabled on every web-capable mode including retrieve, retrieve mode forces search on even when config disables it, and deepresearch/multi can never enable search regardless of config or flags; fetchEnabled requires searchEnabled and additionally needs config.web.fetch.enabled or the --web-fetch flag, and CLI engine/limit/domain overrides fall back to config web.search/web.fetch values.

validateWebOptions rejects two run-time conflicts before dispatch: combining --web-allowed-domains with --web-blocked-domains (error 'Cannot combine ... Use one list only.') and passing --web-fetch while web search is disabled (error 'Flag "--web-fetch" has no effect without web search.').

modelSupportsServerTools returns false for any model starting with 'perplexity/'; assertWebToolsCompatible (called from cli.ts before runMode whenever search or fetch is enabled on a web-allowed mode) resolves the mode's web model and throws `Model <model> does not support OpenRouter server tools. Use a Grok model alias or run with --no-web.` when a Perplexity alias is configured with web on.

buildTools in src/openrouter.ts returns undefined tools for Perplexity models (model.startsWith('perplexity/')) even when web options are enabled, mechanically enforcing the same server-tool incompatibility in the client; the client-side behavior is pinned by tests asserting no tools are attached for perplexity/sonar-reasoning-pro.

resolveWebModel(config, profile, mode) picks the alias for the web-tool compatibility check as role = (mode === 'auto' ? 'expert' : mode) and alias = (role === 'fast' ? 'fast' : 'expert'), so auto routes to the expert alias and only fast routes to the fast alias; the single-call, retrieve, and schema pipeline paths use the same auto→expert / fast→fast / expert→expert alias mapping in src/modes.ts.

runMode dispatches in strict priority order schema → multi → retrieve → deepresearch → single Grok call; auto/fast/expert each make one Grok call (buildSingleCallMessages, temperature 0.2) with OpenRouter web search on by default, while --json combined with web switches the tail to a two-pass research-with-tools then tool-less json_format pattern (2 calls) and --json without web stays a single call.

deepresearch mode makes exactly one Sonar call (role 'deepresearch', buildResearchMessages, temperature 0.2) resolved from the deepResearch alias — perplexity/sonar-deep-research on quality, perplexity/sonar-pro on economy — with Sonar's own native research and no OpenRouter web tools; the deprecated research mode token maps to this same routing.

multi mode is a 5-call ensemble: 1 Sonar research pass using the research alias (perplexity/sonar-reasoning-pro on quality), 3 Grok role analyses (engineering, product, skeptic) and 1 Grok synthesis call using the expert alias, with no leg carrying OpenRouter web tools; analysis legs run in parallel by default but sequentially under --max-cost so budget overruns stop dispatch.

The retrieve path fires for mode retrieve and also for --retrieve or --output results|both on any web-capable Grok mode: one call (role 'retrieve', buildRetrieveMessages, json true, temperature 0.1) emits Tavily-style { results, answer } parsed into searchResults, web search is forced on per resolveWebOptions, and --output both adds a second synthesis call without web tools (2 calls total).

Passing --retrieve or --output results|both to a non-web mode (deepresearch or multi) is ignored with the warning `--retrieve/--output was ignored in <mode> mode; this mode does not use OpenRouter web tools.` and the run proceeds as the normal mode pipeline.

The --web flag is a deprecated no-op: runMode appends the warning 'Flag "--web" is deprecated; web search is on by default. Use --no-web to disable.' to the result warnings while web state is untouched.

When --json is combined with web search, the pipeline never sends one request with both response_format json_object and server tools (observed Grok + web_search garbage JSON like -1.5e-05): it runs a research pass with tools (json false) then a json_format pass without tools (json true, temperature 0.1) built by buildJsonFromResearchMessages, merges usage/sources/warnings, and adds the warning 'Used two-pass --json + web (research then JSON format) to avoid json_object+tools failures.'

The --schema branch takes over the single-call path regardless of mode, resolving the fast alias for fast mode and the expert alias otherwise, and warns '--schema overrides <mode> mode; using a single Grok call with schema-constrained output instead.' when the effective mode is deepresearch or multi; with web enabled it runs a two-pass schema_research (tools) then schema (no tools, json true) sequence, and with web off a single schema call with json_object.

callOpenRouter sends response_format json_object only when call.json is true AND the model supports it (everything except perplexity/ via supportsJsonObjectResponseFormat) AND no server tools were attached; tools and response_format are mutually exclusive in a single request, and Perplexity models never receive response_format.

mapOpenRouterError maps a 404 or tool-use error when tools were requested to `Model does not support OpenRouter server tools: <model>. Use a Grok 4.x model, or run with --no-web.`, giving the same incompatibility guidance at the HTTP layer.

The result normalizers (normalizeResult, normalizeRetrieveResult, normalizeSchemaResult) stamp mode, profile, outputFormat, and web onto every run, re-deriving web from the canonical mode via modeAllowsWeb rather than trusting call.web — non-web modes always report { searchEnabled: false, fetchEnabled: false } — and merge/dedupe the branch, deprecation, x/bookmark, and parse warnings.

The nativeMulti model alias is defined in the quality/economy alias tables but unused by any pipeline branch: multi mode fans out to three single Grok calls via the expert alias instead of the nativeMulti model ID.

When web.searchEnabled is true, cli.ts prints 'hint: OpenRouter web search is enabled (--no-web to disable)' to stderr before the run, so agents see that grounding is active on auto/fast/expert/retrieve runs without inspecting output.

OpenRouter server tools (openrouter:web_search, openrouter:web_fetch) run entirely server-side inside a single HTTP request with no client tool loop, but attaching them adds prompt-token overhead even when the model runs zero searches (~1.8k tokens vs ~140 baseline in the spike), so --no-web is recommended for static or cheap prompts; searches inject context that sharply raises prompt tokens and cost, and engines like Exa or Parallel may bill separately.

Operational mode-choice guidance: use auto/expert/fast for decisions and tradeoffs (web on by default with a stderr hint each run), deepresearch for deep factual research instead of default Grok, multi for multi-perspective synthesis, and retrieve or expert --retrieve for raw Tavily-style results[] suitable as RAG input.
